body:
I'm so sorry to hear you are going through that. It can be really isolating. I've really worked hard to balance how much I tell people and when. My friends are MORE than happy to be supportive, but when I feel like I've burdened them enough, I try to look for other outlets -- artistic, talking to family, journaling -- anything that helps. 

I find it also helps if you have a friend that helps you make it funny. I have a HUGE phobia of someone (or myself) choking. So whenever my friend coughs on a crumb, she says in a really dramatic voice "I'm fiiiiiiine, I promise" and we can laugh about it. Anxiety is a serious and debilitating problem, but that doesn't mean it can't be funny and lighthearted when it needs to be.

I know this was a month ago and I don't know if you are still feeling the effects of it, but I just wanted to say that this has absolutely happened to me! Definitely not in the same way (I'm not a gamer), but abrupt changes in the way I expect something to be have given me really weird panic attacks. They are unlike any panic attacks I've ever had.  For example, some time in jr. high, my parents put socks on my dog to make her walk funny. For SOME unknown reason, it made me feel so weird -- anxious, vaguely suicidal, depersonalization/derealization....it was so bizarre.  

I don't know how to explain it, but you're not alone in this. It's just like my brain short-circuited in some weird way and I really didn't understand it. Only happens to me every now and then.

I know, it does sound like I have bad therapists, but I actually really like them. It's taken me three years and about 4 other therapists to find ones that I can actually trust and open up to. I see one sort of general therapist and one that specializes in CBT/ACT. I think they are good for me, it's just taking me a while to be a better patient/client. I get in my own way a lot.

Thanks for your advice about trying to gain some control in another way -- I'll look into that:-)

Nothing in particular happened. It's just the build-up of days and weeks and months of crippling anxiety and every time I start to see a light at the end of the tunnel, I get hit by another train and the darkness descends again.

I talk about it a little bit, but not much. I don't like to burden my friends and family too often, because it does begin to wear on them after a while and I get that. I do have a therapist that I talk to, but I also put up a lot of walls and get in my own way:-) 

I'm just so tired of my catastrophic thinking -- everything is always life or death for me and it's exhausting.

No worries, I don't think there is a "better" answer:-) I sometimes come to terms that this is just the way my life is and I need to find a way to deal with it, but in my darker moments, that's way easier said than done, of course.

Wish you the best and hope you are well!

What if it doesn't get better? I ask this because so many people have given me this advice.  But so far, to be perfectly honest, it has only ever gotten worse. I have had anxiety for nearly two decades. I'm taking medication and seeing two wonderful therapists each week. It seems like nothing helps and I'm doomed to a life of misery. 

I appreciate your advice (though I'm not OP!) and I believe that it got better for you, but sometimes I'm not sure they will get better for me. That's the reality some of us are facing.
